problem_statement: coreui/coreui-free-bootstrap-admin-template (CoreUI Free Bootstrap Admin Template) is a runnable, production-shaped Bootstrap 5 admin dashboard built with Sass, Babel and a pug/HTML view pipeline that compiles to a fully static dist/. It ships a polished shell: a dark fixed sidebar with grouped navigation, a topbar with account/search, a breadcrumb bar, a widget-card row (Users / Income / Conversion Rate / Sessions), a large Traffic chart, progress groups, a big customer table titled Traffic & Sales, plus dedicated Widgets, Cards and Form-control pages. The problem is that every screen is still generic CoreUI demo scaffolding: the wordmark and page <title> say CoreUI, the dashboard widgets and table use meaningless demo vocabulary (Users / Income / Traffic & Sales / New Clients), the Widgets/Cards/Form pages render nameless 'Widget title', 'Card title' and unlabelled form controls, and none of the pages carry a real product page heading (there is no <h1>/<h2> anywhere). Rework the demo into a single coherent fictional product: Tideglass Console, the operations dashboard for the Tideglass edge-delivery / CDN network. Rebrand the shared shell (sidebar wordmark, topbar, footer, page <title>/meta), reframe the dashboard KPIs and the Traffic & Sales board around edge-delivery concepts (active endpoints, egress spend, cache hit ratio, requests/min, an Edge Traffic chart, and a Traffic & Delivery region board), and give the Overview, Signal Widgets, Console Panels and Route & Origin Settings pages a real semantic page header (<h1> title + <h2> lead) so the site reads as one shipped admin product. Keep the CoreUI Bootstrap layout system, sidebar navigation, breadcrumb, grid, charts, responsive behaviour and the static dist build intact; do not rebuild it into a marketing landing page or a different framework.
required_content: The shared shell (sidebar wordmark, page <title>, meta description, footer) reads as Tideglass Console instead of the CoreUI free Bootstrap admin template demo.

The dashboard Overview reframes the four KPI widget cards around edge-delivery signals (active endpoints, egress spend, cache hit ratio, requests/min) instead of the generic Users/Income/Conversion Rate/Sessions demo labels.

The dashboard Traffic chart and the Traffic & Sales customer table are reframed as an Edge Traffic chart and a Traffic & Delivery region board (Region/POP/Bandwidth/Tier/Last purge) instead of the demo Traffic & Sales / User / Country / Usage vocabulary.

The Overview, Widgets, Cards and Form-control pages each gain a real semantic page header — an <h1> product title (Edge Delivery Overview / Signal Widgets / Console Panels / Route & Origin Settings) plus an <h2> descriptive lead — where the demo pages had no headings.
The Widgets and Cards demo pages are reframed with Tideglass edge vocabulary (Signal Widgets, Edge metric, Console Panels) instead of the nameless Widget title / Card title demo copy.
The CoreUI sidebar navigation, topbar, breadcrumb, footer, Bootstrap grid, charts and every route (Overview, Widgets, Cards, Form controls) remain reachable and functional.
The 390px mobile Overview, the mobile Traffic & Delivery board and the mobile open-sidebar state remain readable with no horizontal overflow and no runtime console/network errors.

The Edge Fabric Status strip must be present and consistent on ALL FOUR admin routes (Overview, Signal Widgets, Console Panels, Route & Origin Settings); it must not silently disappear from the secondary pages.

The strip must carry a Global / Regional scope toggle with a readout that starts at 'Scope: Global fabric'; clicking Regional must move the active button AND re-sync the readout to 'Scope: Regional fabric' (the terminal DOM must reflect the selected scope, not a stale label).

The strip's edge-metric tile row must wrap cleanly at 390px so the Overview and the mobile fabric board have no horizontal overflow; it must stay on the CoreUI ivory / indigo card palette rather than being recoloured into an off-brand block.
design_constraints: Preserve the CoreUI Bootstrap 5 design language: the dark fixed sidebar, topbar, breadcrumb bar, card grid, KPI widget colours, Chart.js charts, table styling, spacing rhythm and light/dark theme support.
Do not convert the admin dashboard into a marketing landing page, a docs site, or a different framework; it must remain a CoreUI Bootstrap admin console.

Use the existing view pipeline and static output: edit the src/views HTML pages (Overview, Widgets, Cards, Form controls) and the shared sidebar/topbar/footer chrome, keeping the sass/babel/vendor build and the compiled dist/ intact.

Reuse the template's own local assets (the src/assets/img avatars, brand svg logo and CoreUI icon set) and Bootstrap type/colour theme; do not introduce external stock imagery, remote fonts, analytics or icon packs.
The new page headers must be real semantic headings (<h1> then <h2>) placed in the page content region so screen structure and the breadcrumb stay coherent.
Sidebar nav, breadcrumb, KPI cards, the Traffic & Delivery table and form controls should keep wrapping cleanly on tablet and 390px mobile rather than colliding or overflowing.

The Edge Fabric Status strip is a shared operational band inside the content region on every admin route; its scope toggle must stay wired to the active scope on every capture, its tiles must wrap on mobile, and it must keep the CoreUI card palette — it must not overflow the mobile viewport or drift off-brand.
state_constraints: desktop_initial captures the current CoreUI demo dashboard: CoreUI wordmark, the Users/Income/Conversion Rate/Sessions KPI cards, a Traffic chart, and the Traffic & Sales customer table, with no <h1>/<h2> page heading.
mobile_initial captures the same dashboard at 390px, where the sidebar collapses off-canvas and the KPI cards and table stack; the rebrand must keep this responsive polish.
desktop_traffic_sales and mobile_traffic_sales scroll to the Traffic & Sales board, which lists generic User/Country/Usage/Payment Method columns rather than any edge-delivery region context.

desktop_widgets, desktop_cards and desktop_form_controls capture the Widgets, Cards and Form-control demo pages, which render nameless Widget title / Card title / unlabelled controls and carry no product page heading.
mobile_sidebar_open captures the dashboard at 390px after toggling the off-canvas sidebar open, exercising the CoreUI navigation shell that must stay intact.

Source inspection confirms the site is generated from the CoreUI src/views HTML pipeline with sass/babel/vendors into a static dist/, using local avatar images and the CoreUI icon set, and that the demo pages have h1=0/h2=0.

change_completion: Overview, Signal Widgets, Console Panels and Route & Origin Settings all contribute to one coherent Tideglass Console edge-delivery product.
The generic Users/Income/Conversion Rate/Sessions KPIs and the Traffic & Sales / New Clients / Widget title demo vocabulary no longer dominate the captured pages.
The CoreUI sidebar navigation, breadcrumb, topbar, footer and every route remain functional across the pages.
Each rebranded page carries a real semantic <h1> title plus an <h2> lead where the demo had no headings.
design_consistency: The rebrand preserves the CoreUI Bootstrap admin identity: dark sidebar, topbar, breadcrumb, KPI card colours, charts, table styling and spacing.
New headings and copy sit inside the existing content region and Bootstrap type scale, so the console still reads as the same template productised.
The result remains a Bootstrap admin dashboard, not a marketing site or a different framework.
regression: The static dist/ still serves every page without a custom dev server or runtime errors.
Overview, Widgets, Cards and Form-control routes remain reachable through the CoreUI sidebar, and the Tideglass brand identity is preserved across the shared shell.
responsive: 390px Overview, the mobile Traffic & Delivery board and the mobile open-sidebar state have no horizontal overflow or collapsed/colliding layout.
Sidebar, breadcrumb, KPI cards, the region table and form controls wrap cleanly on tablet and mobile.

author_notes: Repo-grounded CoreUI Bootstrap admin design_continuity/modify (Edit) task. The static dist/ builds fully offline (npm run build: sass + babel + syncdir views/assets + vendors) and serves clean (0 console, 0 network, 0 overflow) on all eight states. The task asks for a full multi-section, multi-page rebrand of the CoreUI demo into a Tideglass Console edge-delivery admin while preserving the Bootstrap shell, testing layout continuity, content architecture and the addition of real semantic page headings, with no issue/PR framing.

metadata.selected_repo_reason: CoreUI Free Bootstrap Admin Template — a runnable Bootstrap 5 admin dashboard (sass/babel/pug view pipeline to a static dist/) whose every screen is generic CoreUI demo scaffolding; design_continuity modify rebrand into a coherent Tideglass Console edge-delivery admin across the dashboard, widgets, cards and form pages while preserving the CoreUI Bootstrap shell and adding real semantic page headings.
